questions.question: In the remote data logging system, which socket type is used to send sensor data from the client to the server?
questions.explanation: The client creates a UDP socket using socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM) to send the sensor readings to the server.
questions.source: See Lecture 31 (Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi – Part 2) @ 07:10

questions.question: Which Adafruit function is used in the client code to read humidity and temperature values from the DHT sensor?
questions.explanation: The sensordata() function calls Adafruit_DHT.read_retry(sensor,17), which returns the humidity and temperature values from the DHT sensor.
questions.source: See Lecture 31 (Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi – Part 2) @ 04:50

questions.question: Where does the server in the remote data logging example save the data received from the client as mentioned in the lecture?
options: In a text file named Datalog.txt
questions.explanation: The server code opens 'Datalog.txt' in append mode and writes the received message from the client into this text file.
questions.source: See Lecture 31 (Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi – Part 2) @ 15:40

questions.question: Which Python string function is used to split the comma-separated sensor data into separate values on the server?
questions.explanation: The split() function splits a string into multiple strings based on a specified separator/delimiter, e.g. Data.split(",") splits data wherever a comma is found.
questions.source: See Lecture 32 (Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi – Part 3) @ 08:40

questions.question: State whether the following statement is True or False. Statement: Matplotlib Python library is used to plot the temperature and humidity data received at the server in the lecture.
questions.explanation: MATPLOTLIB is a Python library used to create 2D plots; functions such as plot(), xlabel(), ylabel(), and title() are used to plot and label the sensor data.
questions.source: See Lecture 32 (Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi – Part 3) @ 12:15

questions.question: Which matplotlib function turns on interactive mode so that the plot updates in real time as new data arrives?
questions.explanation: ion() turns on the interactive mode in matplotlib. Other common plotting functions mentioned include figure(), grid(), subplot(), close(), and scatter().
questions.source: See Lecture 32 (Implementation of IoT with Raspberry Pi – Part 3) @ 23:25

questions.question: In a traditional (non-SDN) network, where does the routing protocol logic (e.g., OSPF) mainly execute?
questions.explanation: In the current network, protocols like OSPF execute at the switches, which forward traffic in a distributed manner with no centralized control.

questions.question: In which year was the OpenFlow project — from which the idea of software-defined networking originated — presented at ACM SIGCOMM?
questions.explanation: The idea of software-defined networking originated from the OpenFlow project, presented at ACM SIGCOMM in 2008. Stanford published the OpenFlow V1.0.0 specification the following year.

questions.question: What message does a switch send to the SDN controller when it receives a packet for which no matching flow-rule exists?
questions.explanation: When no flow-rule is present for an incoming request, the switch sends a PACKET-IN message to the controller, which then decides a suitable flow-rule and inserts it at the switch.

questions.question: Which SDN API is used for communication between the control layer and the infrastructure layer?
questions.explanation: The Southbound API is used to communicate between the control layer and the infrastructure layer using the OpenFlow protocol. The Northbound API communicates between the control and application layers.

questions.question: According to the lecture, approximately how many requests per second can a typical SDN controller handle through a single thread?
questions.explanation: The lecture states that a controller can typically handle around 200 requests in a second through a single thread.

questions.question: Which control mechanism is described where the entire network's control decisions are taken by a single controller?
questions.explanation: In centralized control, control decisions are taken in a centralized manner by a single controller, unlike distributed control where each subnetwork is controlled by a different controller.

questions.question: Which of the following is listed as a benefit of integrating SDN with IoT?
questions.explanation: Benefits of integrating SDN in IoT include intelligent routing decisions, simplified information collection/analysis/decision-making, visibility of network resources, and intelligent traffic pattern analysis.
questions.source: See Lecture 35 (Software-Defined IoT Networking – Part I) @ 02:50

questions.question: According to the lecture, what is a key resource-constraint challenge in wireless sensor networks that motivates software-defined WSN?
questions.explanation: Wireless sensor network challenges include real-time programming of sensor nodes, vendor-specific architecture, resource-constrained (heavy computation cannot be performed) devices, and limited memory, meaning too many control programs cannot be inserted.
questions.source: See Lecture 35 (Software-Defined IoT Networking – Part I) @ 08:10

questions.question: In the SDN-WISE protocol stack for sensor nodes, what does "INPP" stand for?
questions.explanation: In the SDN-WISE protocol stack, the forwarding layer above IEEE 802.15.4 consists of flow-rules, and INPP stands for In Network Packet Processing.
questions.source: See Lecture 35 (Software-Defined IoT Networking – Part I) @ 15:35
